sentences.text:
This judgment is the outcome of the final report filed by the PI of Halsur Gate Police Station,
Bengaluru against the accused No.1 and 2 for the offences punishable U/s. 420 and 511 R/w 34 of Indian Penal Code.

2. Brief Facts Of The Case Of Prosecution:-
The case of prosecution is that, on 28.07.2017 at about 2.00 pm the accused No.1 and 2 were trying to sell urea to general public near Government Arts College Old Post Office Road, Bengaluru falsely representing as if they are selling Ephedrine narcotic substance with an intention to have personal gain by seeling Urea to general public thereby cheating the general public and committed offence punishable under Sections 420 and 511 R/w 34 of Indian Penal Code.
3.
In response to court summons the accused No.1 and 2 appeared through their counsel Sri. G.S. and have been enlarged on bail.
Cognizance was taken for the alleged C.C. No.14442/2019 offences.
The prosecution papers have been furnished to the accused persons through their counsel as contemplated U/s 207 Cr.P.C. Heard before framing of Charges.
Charges were framed, read over and explained to the accused No.1 and 2 in Kannada language known to them, having understood the same they pleaded not guilty of offence and claimed to be tried.
During pending of this case, the Accused No.1 was reported to be dead and case against the Accused No.1 is abated.
4. As per the charge sheet the prosecution has cited 13 witnesses.
CW.1 is reported to be dead.
CW.4 by name Channappa.
HC is examined as PW.1 and CW.11 by name Suma.
S Scientific expert FSL Bengaluru is examined as PW.2.
In spite of repeated issuance of summons, NBW and proclamation the other other prosecution witnesses were not secure and were dropped.
Ex . P.1
to Ex.P.3
are marked.
5. Statement of accused under Section 313 Crpc was recorded and incriminating evidence in the case of prosecution was read over to the accused persons.
The accused No.1 and 2 have denied the incriminating evidence C.C. No.14442/2019 against them and submitted that, they have no defense evidence.
6. Heard arguments of learned APP for the prosecution and learned counsel for the accused persons.
Perused the entire materials on record.

7. On the basis of the materials on record the following points arise for the consideration:-
1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that on 28.07.2017 at were trying to sell urea to general public near Government Arts College Old Post Office Road, Bengaluru falsely representing as if they are selling Ephedrine narcotic substance with an intention to have personal gain by seeling Urea to general public Anand Kumar Police Inspecter vs Kanthjaraj on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97026467/
2 thereby cheating the general public and thereby accused have committed an offense punishable 420 and 511 R/w 34 of Indian Penal Code?

sentences.text: 2. What order?

8. My answers to the above points are as under:
Point No.1 :- In the Negative Point No.2 :- As per final order for the following:
C.C. No.14442/2019 REASONS 9. REASONING ON POINT NO.1 TO 3 :- The offences alleged against the accused No.2 is punishable under Sections 420 and 511 R/w 34 of Indian Penal Code.

Sec-420. Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property.-- Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
Sec-511. Punishment for attempting to commit offences punishable with imprisonment for life or other imprisonment --

Whoever attempts to commit an offence punishable by this Code with imprisonment for life or imprisonment, or to cause such an offence to be committed, and in such attempt does any act towards the commission of the offence, shall, where no express provision is made by this Code for the punishment of such attempt, be punished with imprisonment of any description provided for the offence, for a term which may extend to one-half of the imprisonment for life or, as the case may be, one-half of the longest term of imprisonment provided for that offence, or with such fine as is provided for the offence, or with both.

10. The case of the prosecution is that, on 28.07.2017 at about 2.00 pm the accused No.1 and 2 were trying to sell urea to general public near Government Arts College Old Post Office Road, Bengaluru falsely representing as if they are selling Ephedrine narcotic substance with an intention to have personal gain by seeling Urea to general public thereby C.C. No.14442/2019 cheating the general public and committed offence punishable under Sections 420 and 511 R/w 34 of Indian Penal Code.
11. To bring home the guilt of the accused persons, the prosecution has examined 02 witness as PW-1 and PW.2 and Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-3 are marked.

12. The CW.4 by name Channappa is examined as examined as PW.2 is deposed that, on 28.07.2017 at 12.00 pm the CW.1 called him and CW.5 to CW.9 to the Police Station and informed then that some persons are selling Ephedrine narcotic substance near Government Arts College Mysore Bank Circle and explained them about the intended raid.

sentences.text: He has further deposed that, he CW.5 to CW.9 and pancha witnesses CW.2 and CW.3 accompanied CW.1 to the said place and reach their at about 2.00 pm.

They found 2 persons who were in possession of suspicious substance and they were Anand Kumar Police Inspecter vs Kanthjaraj on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97026467/
3 seeking customers.

sentences.text: He has further deposed that, immediately they surrounded the accused and apprehended them.

The matter was intimated to CW.10 and CW.10 reached the place of incident and conducted personal search C.C. No.14442/2019 of both the accused and seized two packets of white powder weighing 800 grams with cash of Rs.500/- from accused No.1 and two packets of white powder weighing 20 grams each and Rs.300/- cash from accused No.2.
The CW.10 seized 2 mobile phones from the possession of accused No.1 and 2 and weighed and seized substance at the spot with the help of weighing machine.
The CW.1 conducted mahazar and seized the substance by seeling it with HGC seal.

The PW.1 has identified Ex.P.1.
13.
The CW.11 by name Suma.

S the Scientific expert FSL Bengaluru is examined as PW.2 and she has deposed that, on 01.08.2017 Halasur Gate Police Station had sent two sealed items to their department for chemical analysis in Cr.No. 217/2017.
The seals of the items were intact.
When these items were examined, it was found that there was white powder.
When these items were subjected to chemical testing separately, it was found that the above items contained urea.
She was entered the test method in the form and has given a report in this regard.
The prosecution has produced Exh.P-1 to Exh.P-3.
Exh.P-1 is the mahazar, Exh.P-2 is the report and Exh.P.3 is the seal.
15. As the alleged offenses is with regard to the cheating general public at large, the prosecution ought to have examine the general public if any whom were cheated by the accused.

The entire prosecution case shows that, the FIR was registered against the accused for the offence punishable under Section 9(A), 25(A) of NDPS Act and after investigation charge sheet is filed alleging for the offence punishable under Section 420 and 511 R/w 34 of IPC.
The evidence of PW.1 and PW.2 is not sufficient to hold that the accused has committed the alleged offences.
The prosecution has not explained as to what prevented them from examining the investigating officer to prove guilt of accused.
The prosecution has not examined the investigating officer in this case which is itself fatal to the case of prosecution.
In the absence of cogent evidence the charges levelled against the Accused is not proved by the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt.
Thus in the absence of cogent oral and documentary evidence the prosecution has utterly failed to prove the alleged offenses against the Accused.
Hence Point No.1 is answered in NEGATIVE 17.
POINT NO. 2:-

For the aforesaid reasons, this court proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/s.248(1) of Cr.P.C. accused No.2 is hereby Acquitted of the offences punishable U/s.420 and 511 R/w 34 of Indian Penal Code.
The bail bond and surety bond of the accused No.2 stands cancelled.
